member_targets: The decision process or criteria cooks use to arrive at a station layout suited to a specific menu — i.e., how layout choices are derived (e.g., from analysis of order frequency, work sequence, trial and refinement, training or convention).

The method or decision procedure a cook uses to arrive at an optimal station layout for a given menu — i.e., how layout choices are derived (what information, criteria, or process determines placement), not merely the stated fact that layout is tailored to menu and work sequence.
The set of planning or optimization methods (techniques/approaches) available for determining a kitchen station layout under uncertainty about order mix and sequence.
The set of planning or optimization approaches (methods/techniques) for choosing a station layout under uncertainty about order mix and sequence.

The way menu content determines which items, tools, and ingredients are placed where in the station layout — i.e., the mechanism by which menu-specific dish requirements and work sequence shape placement and reach decisions.
The specific ways cooks modify their station setup (placement, portioning, tool arrangement, quantities) in response to advance knowledge of the expected dish mix.

The specific adaptations cooks make to station layout and prep (which items are portioned, how tools and ingredients are positioned and prioritized) under conditions of known, predictable order mix — i.e., what changes in setup when demand composition is known in advance.

focal_unknown_anchor: When the mix and sequence of orders are unknown in advance, choosing the layout that best balances those competing efficiencies remains a planning problem.
